meaning.cash: Cash and money in bank, savings or deposit accounts. Usually readily accessible, so it counts toward what can be spent this month.
meaning.listed: Listed investments: shares, funds, ETFs and bonds, held directly or through a broker or investing app. Can usually be sold within days; the value moves with the market.
meaning.retirement: Mandatory or workplace retirement savings. Counts toward net worth. Usually locked until the owner is eligible to withdraw, so it does not count toward what can be spent this month unless the holding is marked accessible.
meaning.property: Real estate: a home the user lives in, or a property held to let or as an investment. Counts at its estimated sale value; a loan on it is a separate liability.
meaning.vehicle: A car, motorbike or other vehicle. Counts at its estimated resale value, which usually falls over time; a loan on it is a separate liability.
meaning.equity: Shares or options granted by an employer, such as RSUs or stock options. Vested shares can usually be sold; unvested ones are locked until they vest.
meaning.crypto: Cryptocurrency, on an exchange or in a wallet the user controls. Can usually be sold within days; the value is volatile.
meaning.mortgage: A loan secured on property. A liability: the amount still owed reduces net worth.
meaning.loan: Money owed on a loan other than a mortgage, such as a car, student or personal loan. A liability: the amount still owed reduces net worth.
meaning.wrapper: A tax-advantaged savings or investment account. Whether money can be taken out early without a penalty depends on the account; the holding’s access records which.
meaning.card: A credit card balance. A liability: the amount owed reduces net worth.
meaning.other: Anything the user owns or owes that no other type describes. How accessible it is comes from the user’s own answer.
